title: Numerical Symbolism and the Giants
english: Four hundred sixty-two, one hundred twenty-one, makes the total four hundred forty, being double the one hundred twenty, of which the parts are fifteen, just as fifteen increased by progression makes the one hundred twenty. That the fifteen was received into the most perfect degree is clear; for of that same number six degrees [are missing]. But also the 'giving a portion to the seven', which signifies the Old Testament, and 'also to the eight', which is a symbol of the Resurrection and the New Testament, joins the fifteen. For the Jews, receiving only the old, give a portion to the seven, not hearing that it also gives to the eight; but also the heretics, setting aside the old, giving a portion to the eight, refuse to have the seven provide; the ecclesiastical, receiving both covenants, gives a portion to both. Since therefore also the one hundred twenty number is doubled, there exists a symbol of teaching being awakened toward the true life according to both practice and contemplation, honored, so that having doubled the life, they may have this life, being made manifest through the number, in order that the said thing—that he who lives not also by practice and contemplation does not live, but just as the profligate has died—may be true.

4. And the giants were upon the earth in those days and after that, as the sons of God were approaching the daughters of men and they became to themselves (Gen 6:4). Those were the giants from of old, the men who are named. Those outside the faith, bringing this in from myths, bring it in; but in the Divine Scripture, instead of strong men, they are named. For in Isaiah, God threatening to take away the useful things of these, since they were worthy of this, joins both giant and strong among those being taken away. And Goliath he thus called, testifying that he was strong and a warrior. But also, when Moses wrote out the spies reporting concerning the hostile land, they said concerning the country: “But we saw sons of giants there” (Num 13:34), then interpreting their size they said: “And we were before them as locusts.” Thus it bears witness that they were of great bodies.

And if it has been said aptly that demons used passionate men as instruments, one might say that, to convict them, such great ones were born to them of the most corporeal condition, who were also called “renowned” “from of old,” the “from of old” signifying that the account concerning them as of great bodies is carried for a long time. But if you should also call them giants because of the vileness of their condition, what is said would not be without reason — those who according to wickedness begat those under them, anointing them unto greatness of vileness.

But if the “after that” in the text signifies, besides the time, also the “after the separation from them of the spirit” concerning which God said: “My spirit shall not remain in these men, because they are flesh” (Gen 6:3), consider together: for then, alienated from participation in it, whether men or others, they had offspring raised up against the counsel of God — not only thoughts but also men. Gen 6:5–7. And the Lord God saw that the evils of men were multiplied upon the earth, and that everyone devises in his heart diligently upon evil things all the days; and God considered that he made man upon the earth, and he pondered, and God said: “I will blot out the man whom I made from the face of the earth, from man to cattle and from creeping things to the birds of heaven, because I was angered that I made them.” Consequently, even if the irrational things are not something voluntary […].
